title: Multi-Hop Query Performance, RDBMS vs Graph Database
description: Compare RDBMS join time against graph traversal time from one to five hops, on a log or a linear axis.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Graph Database Architecture

educational.learningObjective: Given response-time data at increasing traversal depth, the learner will explain why RDBMS JOIN cost grows so much faster than graph-database traversal cost as connection depth increases.
prerequisites: Knows what a database join is
learningOutcomes: Explain why join cost compounds with depth while traversal cost does not
Read the same data correctly on both a log and a linear axis
Recognize when a log scale is the honest choice
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to predict the six-hop values for both systems and to say which axis they would use to present the result, and why.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Grouped bar chart with an axis-scale toggle
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Representation contrast - identical data under two scalings
misconceptionsAddressed: That relational and graph databases differ at every query depth
That a log axis is a way of exaggerating a difference
discussionQuestions: When is a logarithmic axis clarifying, and when is it hiding the story?
At what query depth does switching database technology become worth the migration cost?
Why does index-free adjacency make depth nearly free?
